prompt: A vertical 9:16 photograph taken from low down on the floor of a narrow council-flat hallway at dusk, looking along a worn swirl-patterned carpet towards the inside of a white uPVC front door. The brass letterbox flap is still tilted open, and a small pile of junk mail has just landed on a thin brown coir doormat: a pizza menu, a window-cleaning leaflet, a brown envelope, and a glossy flyer face up whose bold white sans-serif headline reads "SPONSOR A CHANCELLOR" above a photo of a well-fed man in his fifties in an expensive camel coat looking mournfully into the lens. The only light is a cold grey-blue dusk coming through the frosted glass panel in the door, with a faint warm amber spill from a living-room doorway off to the left edge of frame. A draught excluder lies along the bottom of the door and a pair of old slippers sits off-centre near the skirting board. Low contrast, lifted blacks, soft and slightly smeared, shot on a consumer phone at night with visible noise and no crisp detail. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 photograph looking straight down at a worn doormat just inside a council flat's front door, framed slightly off-centre so the bottom edge of the white door and a strip of patterned carpet cut into the top of the frame. Scattered across the mat lie a gas bill in a window envelope, a supermarket offers leaflet, a takeaway menu, and a postcard-sized flyer half covered by the menu, with the words "SPONSOR A CHANCELLOR" printed in bold white capitals on a black band and a black-and-white photo of a plump, comfortable middle-aged man in a tailored coat with a trembling, wounded expression. The toe of an old woman's fleece-lined slipper and the hem of her buttoned brown winter coat enter from the bottom edge. Flat, cold blue-grey light from a frosted door pane, very even and shadowless, with one weak warm glow on the carpet from a lamp out of frame. Shot on slightly grainy 1980s colour negative film, muted colours, low contrast. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 close-up photograph of an elderly woman's hand holding a glossy junk-mail flyer at chest height in a dim council-flat hallway, the cuff of her thick buttoned winter coat and the edge of a knitted glove pulled back at the wrist. Her hand is real and old: thin papery skin, liver spots, raised veins, a worn gold wedding ring, short unpainted nails. The flyer reads "SPONSOR A CHANCELLOR" in bold white sans-serif capitals, and under it is a photo of an invented well-fed man in his fifties in a navy cashmere coat, his face even sadder than a charity advert, eyes wet, lower lip unsteady, standing beside a gleaming car. Behind her hand, out of focus, a white uPVC door with a frosted glass panel lets in cold grey-blue dusk, and a warm amber light from another room catches one side of her knuckles. Normal lens, slightly off-centre, soft focus at the edges, low contrast and lifted blacks, like a noisy phone photo taken at night. Thanks.
